interpretability: Kernel-inspired, standard in ML. Activation = distance from zero in feature space.
literary_suitability: Good concept (norm as richness signal) but sigma must match the ||H|| scale.

sensitivity_near_saturation: Avoided by construction: sigma proportional to data scale
critical_point: Maximum sensitivity at ||H_d|| = sigma_d, aligned with data distribution
interpretability: Each dimension sets its own scale. 'How many sigmas from zero?'
literary_suitability: Most appropriate: different literary dimensions have different natural scales.

interpretability: Intuitive: linear scale from 0 to ceiling
literary_suitability: Hard ceiling limits richness for exceptional texts.
Requires meaningful threshold mu per dimension.

interpretability: Squashing function with linear regime near zero.
literary_suitability: Decent but approaches 1 asymptotically; still saturates but more gradually.

formula: a_d = log(1 + exp(||H_d|| / beta)) / log(1 + exp(1/beta))
critical_point: Gradual transition; no single critical point
interpretability: Softplus = smooth ReLU. Less intuitive for similarity.
literary_suitability: Smooth but hard to interpret as a 'richness signal'.
Decent: saturates like RBF but more gradually.

formula: a_d = (1 + cos(pi * ||H_d|| / max_norm)) / 2 for ||H|| < max_norm, else 0
literary_suitability: Not appropriate: cosine is periodic, literary features are not.
